children: New orders for U.S. durable manufactured goods orders edged down $0.1B to $338.6B in August, virtually unchanged on a percentage basis, slowing from 0.9% growth in July (revised from +1.1%), according to data released by the U.S. Census Bureau on Friday. Still, that exceeded the consensus estimate expecting a 0.3% decline.
The barely perceptible dip followed two months of increases. Year to date, new orders for durable goods rose 8.4% from the same period in 2025.
Core durable goods orders, which exclude transportation, grew 0.3%, less than the +0.6% consensus and easing from +0.7% prior (revised from +0.4%).
New orders, excluding defense, edged up 0.1%, decelerating from +1.4% in July (revised from +1.3%).
Transportation equipment, down three of the last four months, drove the weakness in durables' new orders, falling 0.6% to $114.1B

title: Durable goods orders growth stalls in August, better than the decline expected
